rows.citation: Kelly D, Gray R, Shao Y (2011). Examining random and designed tests to detect code mistakes in scientific software. Journal of Computational Science 2(1):47-56.
rows.model_type: general scientific/computational software (non-neuroscience); empirical testing study
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - studies detection of seeded code mistakes, building on Hook's mutation sensitivity testing; full mutation protocol not read (abstract paywalled).
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - compares randomly generated against designed test inputs; inputs are program arguments, not current-clamp stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - outputs are numerical program results compared under tolerances; no electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - compares test-selection strategies (random vs designed) and tolerance levels; no greedy compact battery selection reported.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - abstract/summaries do not report a held-out program set or held-out fault family.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-assisted code changes.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Finds tighter output tolerances matter more than more tests. NeuroSem would calibrate tolerances by numerical refinement, use eFEL feature fingerprints on NeuroML models, select a greedy battery, and test on held-out models and mutation family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1016/j.jocs.2010.12.002 (title, 3 authors, J Comput Sci vol 2 pp 47-56, 2011); Semantic Scholar API (TLDR; abstract elided); web search summary of abstract.

rows.citation: Hook D, Kelly D (2009). Mutation Sensitivity Testing. Computing in Science & Engineering 11(6):40-47.
rows.model_type: numerical scientific software without exact oracles (non-neuroscience)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - seeds code mutants into scientific code to measure how sensitive a test set is to faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - uses sets of test inputs (hand-picked and random) but not stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares numerical outputs under error tolerances; no electrophysiology.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - argues a few well-designed tests detect many faults and tolerance reduction beats more tests; no formal greedy selection found.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out models or held-out mutation family reported in abstract.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest scientific-computing precedent for mutant-based test sensitivity with tolerances. NeuroSem applies the idea to NeuroML/LEMS neurons with current-clamp protocols, eFEL fingerprints, refinement-calibrated tolerances, greedy battery selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1109/mcse.2009.200 (title, 2 authors, CiSE vol 11 pp 40-47, Nov 2009); OpenAlex abstract (W2031588966).

rows.citation: Hansel D, Mato G, Meunier C, et al. (1998). On Numerical Simulations of Integrate-and-Fire Neural Networks. Neural Computation 10(2):467-483.
rows.model_type: integrate-and-fire neuron networks
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - varies integration scheme and time step, a numerical perturbation, but not a systematic single-fault mutation framework.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - focus is network synchronization under integration settings, not multiple clamp protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - assesses synchronization properties of spiking; no eFEL-style single-cell feature fingerprints.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - proposes an improved integration scheme; no protocol selection.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows Euler/RK2 step size silently alters network behaviour and proposes a fix. NeuroSem would treat such numerical changes as one mutation family and use refinement to calibrate detection tolerances.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1162/089976698300017845 (title, 4 authors, Neural Comput vol 10 pp 467-483, 1998, abstract).

rows.citation: Just R, Jalali D, Inozemtseva L, et al. (2014). Are mutants a valid substitute for real faults in software testing? Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Foundations of Software Engineering (FSE 2014), pp. 654-665.
rows.model_type: general software (5 open-source Java applications, 357 real faults)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - uses systematically seeded syntactic mutants and correlates their detection with real-fault detection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - software test suites, not stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - evaluates mutant validity, controlling for coverage; no suite minimisation.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - real developer-fixed faults act as an external check on mutant-based conclusions, not a held-out mutation family.
rows.software: none (Defects4J faults used; tool URL not retrieved here)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Supports using mutants as fault proxies in general software. NeuroSem would need an analogous validity argument for neuron-model mutations and adds held-out mutation-family evaluation in a neuroscience setting.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1145/2635868.2635929 (title, 6 authors, FSE 2014 pp 654-665); OpenAlex abstract (W2135937266).

rows.citation: Ammann P, Delamaro ME, Offutt J (2014). Establishing Theoretical Minimal Sets of Mutants. 2014 IEEE Seventh International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation (ICST), pp. 21-30.
rows.model_type: general software mutation analysis (benchmark programs)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - analyses generated mutants and redundancy among them.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - test cases, not stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - minimises the mutant set relative to a test set; the dual of NeuroSem's test-battery minimisation.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Minimises mutants given tests using subsumption. NeuroSem minimises the protocol battery given mutants, with feature-based kill criteria and held-out evaluation, in neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1109/icst.2014.13 (title, 3 authors, ICST 2014 pp 21-30); OpenAlex abstract (W2008479535).

rows.citation: Inozemtseva L, Holmes R (2014). Coverage is not strongly correlated with test suite effectiveness. Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE 2014), pp. 435-445.
rows.model_type: general software (large Java programs)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - uses mutation score as the measure of suite effectiveness.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - test suites of varied size, not stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - samples many suites of differing size and coverage; does not optimise a compact suite.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Warns that coverage and suite size confound effectiveness. NeuroSem would compare a selected battery against size-matched random batteries, measured on mutated neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1145/2568225.2568271 (title, 2 authors, ICSE 2014 pp 435-445); OpenAlex abstract (W2106072155).

rows.citation: Nemhauser GL, Wolsey LA, Fisher ML (1978). An analysis of approximations for maximizing submodular set functions-I. Mathematical Programming 14:265-294.
rows.model_type: combinatorial optimisation theory (submodular set functions)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - theoretical optimisation paper.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - none.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - proves greedy selection achieves a (1-1/e)-type approximation for monotone submodular maximisation.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Foundational guarantee for greedy coverage-style selection. NeuroSem only uses greedy selection as one component and would cite this for the approximation bound, not as an overlapping method.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1007/bf01588971 (title, 3 authors, Math Program vol 14 pp 265-294, Dec 1978); Semantic Scholar TLDR (abstract elided).

rows.citation: Godlin B, Strichman O (2009). Regression verification. Proceedings of the 46th Annual Design Automation Conference (DAC 2009), pp. 466-471.
rows.model_type: general programs (successive versions)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares closely related program versions, not seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - formal equivalence proof, no test inputs.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Proves equivalence of program versions formally. NeuroSem makes only empirical, tolerance-based behavioural-equivalence judgements for neuron models and does not claim proofs.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1145/1629911.1630034 (title, 2 authors, DAC 2009 pp 466-471); OpenAlex abstract (W2293092623).

rows.citation: Person S, Dwyer MB, Elbaum S, et al. (2008). Differential symbolic execution. Proceedings of the 16th ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Foundations of Software Engineering (FSE 2008), pp. 226-237.
rows.model_type: general programs (version differencing)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - characterises real code changes between versions.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - symbolic execution rather than concrete stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Characterises semantic effects of code changes symbolically. NeuroSem characterises effects of model changes by simulation under stimuli with feature fingerprints; different technique and domain.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1145/1453101.1453131 (title, 4 authors, FSE 2008 pp 226-237); OpenAlex abstract fragment (W2074888021).

rows.citation: Abbas H, Mittelmann H, Fainekos G (2014). Formal property verification in a conformance testing framework. 2014 Twelfth ACM/IEEE Conference on Formal Methods and Models for Codesign (MEMOCODE), pp. 155-164.
rows.model_type: cyber-physical system models (e.g. Simulink models and derived implementations)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - compares an original model with a derived (simplified or implemented) model, not seeded single faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - closeness is a distance between output trajectories over inputs; approximated computationally.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - trajectory distances and temporal-logic properties, not electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - computes closeness; no test battery selection.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Offers a conformance-distance notion between related dynamical models. NeuroSem uses feature-based distances with refinement-calibrated tolerances for neuron models, plus battery selection and held-out mutation evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1109/memcod.2014.6961854 (title, 3 authors, MEMOCODE 2014 pp 155-164); OpenAlex abstract (W2054704105).

rows.citation: Qi Z, Long F, Achour S, et al. (2015). An analysis of patch plausibility and correctness for generate-and-validate patch generation systems. Proceedings of the 2015 International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis (ISSTA 2015), pp. 24-36.
rows.model_type: general software (C programs; automated program repair)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - analyses automatically generated patches (program modifications), not controlled seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - validation test suites, not stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - checks reported patches for correctness beyond the validation suite, exposing weak test oracles.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - automated (search-based, not ML/LLM) program transformations.
rows.software: Kali (described in paper; URL not retrieved)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows weak test suites accept incorrect automated changes. NeuroSem aims to build a stronger protocol battery for judging model transformations, including optional AI-assisted ones, in neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1145/2771783.2771791 (title, 4 authors, ISSTA 2015 pp 24-36); OpenAlex abstract (W2153881107).

rows.citation: Yu B, Zhu Y, He P, et al. (2025). UTBoost: Rigorous Evaluation of Coding Agents on SWE-Bench. arXiv:2506.09289 (journal-ref: ACL 2025).
rows.model_type: LLM coding agents on real-world Python repositories (SWE-Bench)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - evaluates agent-generated patches, not controlled seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - augments tests with LLM-generated unit tests to exercise patches more thoroughly.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - test augmentation to expose insufficient tests; no compact-battery selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out split described in abstract.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - judges AI-generated code patches and uses an LLM to generate tests.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows insufficient tests let wrong AI patches pass. NeuroSem addresses the analogous risk for neuron models using stimulation protocols, eFEL features and calibrated tolerances rather than unit tests.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abs page 2506.09289 (citation_title, 4 authors, date 2025-06-10, jref ACL 2025, abstract).

rows.citation: Chou CJ, Lwin KT, Soremekun E (2026). MUCOCO: Automated Consistency Testing of Code LLMs. arXiv:2604.19086 (arXiv comment: accepted to EMNLP Findings 2026).
rows.model_type: code LLMs (4 coding tasks, 7 LLMs)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - applies semantic-preserving program mutations and checks behaviour consistency against the original.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - compares outputs and test results across mutant programs; not stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out mutation family reported in abstract.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - targets inconsistency of LLM-produced code behaviour.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Uses equivalence-preserving mutants to test LLMs. NeuroSem uses behaviour-changing single faults in NeuroML neurons to select and validate a protocol battery; AI is optional there.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abs page 2604.19086 (citation_title, 3 authors, submitted 2026-04-21, comments field, abstract).

rows.citation: Oberkampf WL, Trucano TG (2002). Verification and validation in computational fluid dynamics. Progress in Aerospace Sciences 38(3):209-272.
rows.model_type: computational fluid dynamics simulations (review)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - review of V&V methods; no seeded faults found in abstract.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - none specific.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: General V&V framework, including numerical error estimation. NeuroSem borrows the refinement idea for tolerances but targets detection of model changes in neuron models, not CFD validation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1016/s0376-0421(02)00005-2 (title, 2 authors, Prog Aerosp Sci vol 38 pp 209-272, 2002); Semantic Scholar abstract/TLDR.

rows.citation: Rotter S, Diesmann M (1999). Exact digital simulation of time-invariant linear systems with applications to neuronal modeling. Biological Cybernetics 81:381-402.
rows.model_type: linear time-invariant systems; integrate-and-fire neurons
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - compares exact integration with multi-purpose solvers across step sizes; numerical variation, not fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - supports general input classes including delta-pulse trains; not a clamp protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - evaluates subthreshold dynamics and spike-timing error.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Provides an exact-integration reference and solver error comparisons. NeuroSem would use such references for tolerance calibration within a broader mutation-and-battery framework.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1007/s004220050570 (title, 2 authors, Biol Cybern vol 81 pp 381-402, 1999); Europe PMC abstract.

rows.citation: Marder E, Goaillard J-M (2006). Variability, compensation and homeostasis in neuron and network function. Nature Reviews Neuroscience 7:563-574.
rows.model_type: review of experimental and theoretical neuron/circuit studies (invertebrates and vertebrates)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - review; discusses conductance variability rather than seeded model faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - not a methods paper.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - discusses how similar activity arises from different conductance combinations.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Background on degeneracy: different parameters can give similar behaviour, implying some mutations may be undetectable. NeuroSem would need to handle such near-equivalent mutants explicitly.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1038/nrn1949 (title, 2 authors, Nat Rev Neurosci vol 7 pp 563-574, 2006); Europe PMC abstract.

rows.citation: Izhikevich EM (2004). Which Model to Use for Cortical Spiking Neurons? IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks 15(5):1063-1070.
rows.model_type: spiking and bursting point-neuron models (review/comparison)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares model families, no fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - model comparison relies on reproducing firing behaviours under various inputs; not a formal protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - qualitative firing-pattern repertoire, not eFEL feature vectors.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Qualitative comparison of neuron model plausibility and cost. NeuroSem instead tests whether specific model edits change behaviour, quantitatively and with calibrated tolerances.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1109/tnn.2004.832719 (title, 1 author, IEEE TNN vol 15 pp 1063-1070, Sep 2004); OpenAlex abstract.

rows.citation: Teeter C, Iyer R, Menon V, et al. (2018). Generalized leaky integrate-and-fire models classify multiple neuron types. Nature Communications 9.
rows.model_type: GLIF point-neuron models fit to 645 Allen Cell Types recordings
rows.controlled_mutations: no - model complexity levels are compared, but no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - fits and evaluates models on multiple stimulus types, with prediction on hold-out stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - compares GLIF parameters against electrophysiological features for cell-type classification; spike-train prediction metrics.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - evaluates on held-out stimuli, not held-out models or mutation families.
rows.software: Allen SDK (https://github.com/AllenInstitute/AllenSDK); link not checked in this paper
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Model fitting and classification from multi-stimulus data. NeuroSem instead detects controlled changes in existing models and optimises the stimulus battery for that.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1038/s41467-017-02717-4 (title, 12 authors, Nat Commun vol 9, Feb 2018, abstract); Semantic Scholar record.

rows.citation: Nandi A, Chartrand T, Van Geit W, et al. (2022). Single-neuron models linking electrophysiology, morphology, and transcriptomics across cortical cell types. Cell Reports 40:111176.
rows.model_type: all-active biophysical multicompartment models of mouse visual cortex neurons (9,200 models from 230 cells)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - sensitivity analysis perturbs conductances about optimised values (Sobol); not single-fault mutation for test assessment.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - uses standardized step, ramp and colored-noise current protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - fits models to electrophysiological features using BluePyOpt and eFEL.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - optimises model parameters, not the stimulation battery.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - validates on noise stimuli excluded from training; held-out stimuli rather than held-out mutation families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - evolutionary optimisation, no AI model transformations.
rows.software: All-active Workflow with BluePyOpt (https://github.com/BlueBrain/BluePyOpt) and eFEL (https://github.com/BlueBrain/eFEL)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares eFEL features, multi-protocol stimulation and held-out-stimulus validation, but for parameter fitting. NeuroSem repurposes these for detecting controlled model faults and selecting a compact battery.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111176 (title, 15 authors, Cell Rep vol 40 art 111176, Aug 2022); OpenAlex abstract; Europe PMC full text PMC9793758 (methods, key resources table).

rows.citation: Kreuz T, Chicharro D, Houghton C, et al. (2013). Monitoring spike train synchrony. Journal of Neurophysiology 109(5):1457-1472.
rows.model_type: spike train data (seizure recordings, model EEG)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - none.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - none.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - defines improved and real-time SPIKE-distance measures of spike train dissimilarity, not eFEL features.
rows.software: none (SPIKE-distance implementations exist; URL not checked here)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Provides a candidate spike-train distance. NeuroSem could use such a metric alongside eFEL fingerprints but otherwise shares none of the pipeline.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1152/jn.00873.2012 (title, 5 authors, J Neurophysiol vol 109 pp 1457-1472, Mar 2013, abstract).

rows.citation: Gleeson P, Steuber V, Silver RA (2007). neuroConstruct: A Tool for Modeling Networks of Neurons in 3D Space. Neuron 54(2):219-235.
rows.model_type: conductance-based multicompartment neuron networks in 3D, NeuroML-based
rows.controlled_mutations: no - GUI model editing, no systematic fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - supports stimulation setups; not a protocol battery for testing changes.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - compares simulated properties with experimental measurements and across simulators.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Cross-simulator checks of NeuroML models by reproducing published results. NeuroSem systematises change detection with mutations, eFEL fingerprints, calibrated tolerances and battery selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1016/j.neuron.2007.03.025 (title, 3 authors, Neuron vol 54 pp 219-235, Apr 2007); OpenAlex abstract.

rows.citation: arbor-sim (2018-). NSuite: benchmarks and numerical validation for multi-compartment neural simulators. GitHub repository.
rows.model_type: multicompartment neuron simulators (Arbor, NEURON, CoreNEURON); validation models include rallpack1, cable steady-state, RC synapse models
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - simulator tags (e.g. NEURON first-order solver) vary numerics; no single-fault model mutation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - each validation model runs one or more parameter sets; not a current-clamp protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares output variables to reference solutions by absolute/relative error thresholds.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Validates simulators against reference solutions with fixed thresholds. NeuroSem validates model changes, with refinement-derived tolerances, feature fingerprints, selected batteries and held-out mutations.
rows.verification_method: GitHub API repos/arbor-sim/nsuite (created 2018-06-11, description); readme.md and docs/validation.rst via GitHub contents API; validation directory listing.

rows.citation: Tiwari K, Kananathan S, Roberts MG, et al. (2021). Reproducibility in systems biology modelling. Molecular Systems Biology 17(2).
rows.model_type: published mathematical systems biology models (BioModels curation)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - reproduction attempts, not seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - none.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - none.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Assesses model reproducibility and proposes a scorecard. NeuroSem instead tests whether model edits are behaviourally detectable; related only as motivation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.15252/msb.20209982 (title, 14 authors, Mol Syst Biol vol 17, Feb 2021, abstract); OpenAlex abstract.

rows.citation: Kiar G, Chatelain Y, de Oliveira Castro P, et al. (2021). Numerical uncertainty in analytical pipelines lead to impactful variability in brain networks. PLOS ONE 16(11):e0250755.
rows.model_type: structural connectome estimation pipeline (brain imaging)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - injects random numerical noise via Monte Carlo Arithmetic; numerical perturbation, not single faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - none.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - connectome features, not electrophysiology.
rows.software: none (Monte Carlo Arithmetic tooling not verified here)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Quantifies numerical instability in a neuroimaging pipeline. NeuroSem uses numerical variation to set tolerances for detecting deliberate edits in neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1371/journal.pone.0250755 (title, 9 authors, PLOS ONE vol 16 e0250755, 2021); OpenAlex abstract.
